clue.text: Mole has to pause for refreshment by the river

parts.note: a tea break or coffee break is a pause for refreshment
water can mean a river or stream, as in the Scottish Water of Leith

explanation.surface: Someone stops for a drink beside the river, and the mole is involved somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the burrowing animal, but here it is a stone pier or sea wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a massive stone pier built out into the sea to shelter a harbour from waves.

clue.text: Palm oil sent up north

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: attar is a fragrant oil from rose petals
N is north

explanation.surface: Palm oil is shipped to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses ATTAR to RATTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing palm whose stems are used in cane furniture.

clue.text: A job the malign goddess found for a defector

parts.note: a post is a job
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A spiteful deity finds work for a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons a religion, party or cause is a renegade.

clue.text: Fashion springing first from a 27 city

indicators.note: first says springing comes before fashion

parts.note: welling means springing up, as water from the ground
ton is fashion, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: A new trend begins in a city of the antipodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is NEW ZEALAND, whose capital this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the island nation at 27 across.

clue.text: Name under which I note "boring type"

indicators.note: in a down clue, under which says the following pieces sit below name

parts.note: a term is a name for something
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone labels a person as tedious company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring type' suggests a dull person, but it is an insect that bores through wood.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects tunnel through timber, so they are borers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Cartel publicising an engagement, perhaps

explanation.surface: A business group announces a betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: A cartel or gang is a ring; a betrothal is shown by the band on the finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A combine of traders fixing prices is one sense; the other is the band worn to show a couple are engaged.

clue.text: Fare vehicle mostly seen in the West Indies

parts.note: to fare is to do, as in how are you doing

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a minicab is a small taxi

explanation.surface: A taxi is spotted in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a taxi passenger but is the verb, meaning get on. A minicab is a British private hire car.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island nation lying among the Windward Islands.

clue.text: Indignation expressed by people in squalid northern street

indicators.note: in says people sit inside the rearranged letters
squalid suggests something run-down and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: N is northern
men are people

explanation.surface: Anger voiced by those living in a grim street in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squalid' gives RESENTT, the jumble of N and the street word, and 'in' sets the people inside it before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter anger at unfair treatment is the meaning of both words.

clue.text: Fashionable quality of sound to voice in the office

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
tone is the quality or timbre of a sound

explanation.surface: A trendy timbre suits someone reading aloud at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The office' is not a workplace: it is a church service (the daily office), whose prayers are chanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To chant prayers in a monotone, as a priest does at a liturgical service called the office.

clue.text: He ma play to students in a different resort

indicators.note: in says the students sit inside the reworked letters of resort
a different resort is the word resort made into something else, its letters rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate, so two students are LL

explanation.surface: A performer entertains students at some other holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' jumbles the resort word into STROER, and 'in' sets the two learners inside it, ahead of ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller was a strolling player, an actor who wandered from town to town giving performances.

clue.text: Organ with potentially explosive contents

parts.note: an organ is a publication such as a periodical, which may carry sensational stories; a store for gunpowder and shells has truly explosive contents

explanation.surface: A body part that might blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests anatomy or a church instrument, but it means a periodical, and the second sense is an ammunition store.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a periodical publication and a store for ammunition share this name, so either reading of the clue fits.

clue.text: Her name appears in some articles

indicators.note: appears in says the name stands inside the articles

parts.note: an and a are both indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A woman is mentioned in a few newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces but means the grammatical words AN and A, with N between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Her stands for any girl's name, and this is a common female forename.

clue.text: Boy seen on site of allotment

parts.note: Al is a short boy's name
a location is a site

explanation.surface: A lad is spotted at his garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment in Britain is a rented garden plot, but here it means a share handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A share given out is what an apportioning produces.

clue.text: Linnaeus, perhaps, anticipating Zola?

explanation.surface: The Swedish botanist seems to foreshadow a French novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Linnaeus classified plants; Zola led the literary school of Naturalism, so a writer of that school before him would be one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Linnaeus was a student of plants and animals, and a writer of the realist school Zola led bore the same name.

clue.text: Coming round again about races, say?

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be pronounced

parts.note: a race is a strong current of water, as in a mill race

explanation.surface: A punter discusses racing again.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening once more, a repetition of something.

clue.text: No restrictions in this Hall. Hardcastle said

explanation.surface: A character in a play declares a house free of rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In Goldsmith's She Stoops to Conquer, Mr Hardcastle tells his guests 'This is Liberty Hall', a place where they may do as they please.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom from restraint is the plain sense; the second is the word Hardcastle puts before Hall in Goldsmith's comedy.

clue.text: Mad about boss building supply vessels

indicators.note: about says mad wraps around boss

parts.note: bats is slang for mad
an umbo is the central boss of a shield

explanation.surface: An angry builder shouts at the manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager but is the raised knob on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: Small boats that bring provisions out to ships lying offshore.

clue.text: A church gallery used for making records

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery in a church is used as a recording studio.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'A', not the '4' of the text held. The Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose acetate was the material of lacquer discs cut in studios as master recordings.

clue.text: Feature of stern uncommonly fat woman

indicators.note: uncommonly means fat appears in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: frail is old slang for a woman, as in frailty, thy name is woman

explanation.surface: A severe expression on a remarkably large lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like severe but is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail around the back of a ship's poop deck.

clue.text: Broadcast version of Webster

indicators.note: a version of something is a rendering of it, here the name rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio adaptation of a dictionary maker or a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' means scatter seed, not air on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter something about, as a sower casts seed.

clue.text: Seize creatures on what is said to be public land

indicators.note: what is said to be signals that the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a common is a stretch of land open to everyone in a village
deer are the grazing creatures

explanation.surface: Someone grabs animals grazing on open ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what is said to be' applies to the public land: a common, open land free to all in British villages, is heard and written COMMAN, with the creatures after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take possession of something by force or official authority, as an army takes vehicles.

clue.text: Immovable season of abstinence

explanation.surface: A fixed period of self-denial, like a feast date that never moves.
explanation.walkthrough: Easter-linked fasts move about the calendar; the surface plays on an 'immovable' one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed firmly is one sense; a period of going without food, as in Lent, is the other.

clue.text: Hot part of Bristol engineering works

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie within the words Bristol engineering

explanation.surface: A heated section of a factory in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' means taken unlawfully, as in hot goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for goods acquired by theft.

clue.text: Small fish from centre of Austrian market

indicators.note: centre of picks the two middle letters of the eight-letter word Austrian

parts.note: an outlet is a market for goods

explanation.surface: A fish bought in the middle of a Viennese market.
explanation.definitionFit: A young trout, the diminutive ending -let marking it as little.

clue.text: Snug the joiner's sign

explanation.surface: A carpenter's shop board.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Snug the joiner plays this animal in the mechanicals' play; Leo is the zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Snug plays the big cat; Leo, a zodiac sign, is that beast too.

clue.text: Such accommodation for new leader of legislature at Be Berne

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head of parliament arriving in the Swiss capital needs somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges L, AT and BERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging that is available to let can be hired for a fee.

clue.text: Book to ring tax firm back

indicators.note: back says the whole string of pieces is read from the end

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
VAT is value added tax
CO is company, a firm

explanation.surface: A ledger is used to phone an accountancy firm in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses OVATCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A book size made by folding each printed sheet into eight leaves.

clue.text: Unaccustomed enthusiasm also observed in the Commonwealth?

parts.note: new to something means unaccustomed to it
zeal is fervent enthusiasm
and means also

explanation.surface: Fresh keenness is noticed among the member nations.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific nation is a member of the Commonwealth of former British territories.
